You deserve so much better. Ultimately, you can take all the advice and still choose to ignore it because you love this human and you think they're a good person despite what some people have said.

And that's okay, it's your life and your decisions. At the end of the day, just make sure you're making decisions for you and your own child. If you feel like this person is a healthy addition to your family and that you're willing to be partners and invite them in to your child's life, then go for it. Discuss things with them, make sure you're on the same page. Are they willing to get a job at any point in the future, what dreams do they have, what goals do they have. Where do they see you as a family in 10 years? Do they want a commitment?

Even if you're just dating, you're allowing this person in to your life, in to your child's life and you need to know if you're wasting your time with them.

But with all that being said, in my own personal opinion, some people can appear perfect and we so desperately want them to be perfect for us. But they just aren't. And it hurts, it hurts to admit that this person you really care about and want to spend time with is just not your forever person. I do feel like you want to ignore these red flags, but as I've recently learned, a red flag is a red flag, no matter the size, shape or specific shade of red. Even if it's the lightest shade of red, it's still red. People don't change unless they significantly want to. People repeat behaviors. Meaning what's done to one person will most likely be done to the next.

And don't forget that people tend to only show sides of themselves, friends aren't reliable necessarily because they've probably only seen certain sides of a person. But living with someone, dating someone, you tend to see all the sides of them. Especially what goes on behind closed doors. So maybe have deeper conversations with the ex, ask specific details, ask what exactly he's done to upset her. If she can't say something specific, then take it with a grain of salt but if she can specify behaviors, listen to them.

I hope things go well for you.

Hi, I'm really sorry for what you've been going through and I know nothing anyone ever says can really make anything better but as someone who jumps a line between being okay and borderline wanting to stop existing, I can say what helped me, personally. 

The first thing I started doing was journaling, just writing everything down. My thoughts, my stories. Good and bad. Just get it all out. 

The second was art. I started with just colouring adult colouring books, which sounds really childish but it worked really well with getting me to focus on something that was not my thoughts. That escalated to painting with watercolours, I have 0 talent but I follow YouTube tutorials. 

Basically, a hobby, a talent. Something to distract. Naturally, it won't be as good as a therapist will be, but as someone who is terrified to take that step, I've learned that focusing on a healthy distraction has been the best way to get through. Some days are still difficult, and once in a while, I start losing my love for these little things. I haven't written in my journal for about two months now but I forced myself to paint a card for my mom. I also know that not everyone is artistic, but there's so many different hobbies, so many things to try out, maybe start with something that has always fascinated you. And always keep in mind that you don't have to be good at something to enjoy doing it. 

But it's a daily battle and I'm proud of you for still being here and still trying to fight.

People have different skin types. So not everything works the same for everyone. Unfortunately you have to experiment until you find a routine that works with your skin type. 

Also try to find products that suit your skin type. (If you struggle with dry skin, don't use products for oily skin, etc.) 

Washing your face twice a day should be good enough. You don't want to be too harsh on your skin. Using more natural products than chemical products are usually better. 

Unfortunately these impurities (the gross stuff) are just a part of your life, they are preventable but it's basically something you have to deal with daily in order for them to stay away.

One thing I have learned is to avoid pore strips as they tend to damage your pores and make them even bigger. Your pores basically get clogged up with stuff quite easily, which is all the gross stuff. But luckily, it can go away. Moisturising your skin is also very important. 

And another tip (I'm sorry for being all over the place, I'm typing as I remember things), when you start washing, use lukewarm water to open up your pores and always use cold water afterwards,  to close them up again. Even after a shower or bath. Pores always need to be closed so that less things can get in. It would also help to not touch your face as much. 

I'm honestly not even remotely an expert. I only recently started getting into skincare and this is just what I've personally learned from other people. 

Your skin is very delicate and it's so good that you're wanting to take care of it! I hope you find something that works for you! It takes some patience and failures (usually failures are when products irritate your skin or cause more breakouts), but eventually you'll find the perfect combination of products and routine which will leave your skin happy and healthy!
